chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Mazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'During the days of Abdullah ibn Ali, these people disputed among themselves.' So he said, 'Leave that aside. The spoiling of their affair will come from where their success began.'

key_terms.عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ: Abdullah ibn Ali (a key Abbasid figure)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the source of the Abbasids' decline?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the root of the Abbasid decline as an internal paradox, where the seeds of their eventual corruption were sown within the very mechanisms of their initial rise to power. This insight highlights the Shia scholarly view that political legitimacy is fragile when internal contradictions, such as hypocrisy or injustice, are embedded in the foundation of authority.

en.hubeali: H 14705 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al-Mufazzal Bin Mazeed, who has narrated the following:

I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The days of Abdullah Bin Ali, they (Abbasid rulers) disputed regarding what was in between them’. So heasws said: ‘You leave that. But rather, the spoiling of their command would come from where their success began’.
en.sarwar: 257. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al-Mufazzal Bin Mazeed, who has narrated the following:

I said to Abu Abdullah (a.s.), ‘The days of Abdullah Bin Ali, they (Abbasid rulers) disputed regarding what was in between them’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘You leave that. But rather, the spoiling of their command would come from where their success began’.
